newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Sverdlovsk sees Eurobond launch by August.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Sverdlovsk sees Eurobond launch by August.

text.p: Sverdlovsk region could be ready to start presenting its planned $100 million Eurobond to potential foreign investors in two months time but is still waiting for official permission to issue the bonds, a senior regional official said on Thursday.

"We've now started parallel work on getting ratings and since we're working on them in tandem, we can probably move into the starting blocks in two months," Galina Kovalyova, deputy chairman of the Sverdlovsk regional government, told Reuters.
She said Standard & Poor's and Moody's were working on the rating. But she said the start date would depend on whether President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree allowing the region to issue the bonds.

Yeltsin signed a decree last month allowing the cities of Moscow and St Petersburg and Nizhny Novorod region to issue Eurobonds but placed certain limits on the issues and stipulated they must obtain two international credit ratings.
The decree made no mention of several other regional governments planning Eurobonds.
She said she did not expect Sverdlovsk to receive ratings lower than the BB- Russia received from Standard & Poor's and the Ba2 it received from Moody's for its two sovereign Eurobond issues.
WestMerchant Bank is lead managing the issue with Russian Inkombank advising on the Russian side.
Sverdlovsk plans to issue $100 million in six- to seven-year bonds initially, bringing total issues to $300 million over several years.
